object_description: two-height volume with plinth and tower
design_condition: The volume fills the southern triangular plot while splitting its height to reduce the perceived impact toward the historic complex and the river.

positive.statement: The differentiated heights contain the volumetric impact toward the historic sector and the river.
The interventions on the historic buildings are respectful and engage with existing elements.
The continuous greenery connects the school park with the river and supports façade shading.
The generous openings integrate the site into neighborhood routes and improve permeability.
The hierarchy of public spaces is a clear and shared intention.
The envelope and plant concept are clear and support the required energy standard.
The observations on material sustainability are sufficiently exhaustive.

negative.statement: The relationship between the plinth and tall building is disproportionate, and the tower geometries are doubtful.
The expression is very closed and has an almost repulsive effect toward the outside.
The spatial organization and access to vertical distribution remain unresolved.
The living area suffers from its placement within the plinth.
The abstract monumental plinth makes dialogue with the historic buildings almost impossible.
The very small windows can be read as a refusal of dialogue with the life and vitality of the historic complex.
The external paving is not completely convincing, while the generous terrace lacks sufficient planning.
The complex geometry complicates the construction details.
